episodes.192478: Scattered to numerous strong thunderstorms developed along a stationary frontal boundary stretching from northwestern Alabama into southeastern Alabama during the afternoon hours. A few of these storms produced strong wind gusts caused isolated wind damage in Colbert county.
episodes.192924: An area of thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall that resulted in flash flooding in the Hereford area.
episodes.192990: Slow moving thunderstorms produced localized flash flooding across the area.
episodes.193131: Sufficient moisture in combination with a shortwave impulse brushing by the area resulted in numerous strong thunderstorm wind gusts in addition to isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.193217: Storms developed over the Nebraska panhandle during the afternoon with hail and strong winds eventually forming into a convective line that propagated into central Nebraska. Additional storms with strong winds moved east out of Wyoming into western Nebraska bringing another round of strong winds into the evening.
episodes.193218: Storms with gusty winds developed early in the afternoon across southeast to south-central Wyoming before organizing into a convective line moving west to east across the area. Strong winds up to 70 mph were reported with these storms.
episodes.193321: The late afternoon sea breeze and boundary mergers focused across the St. Johns River basin across downtown Jacksonville. Slow moving storms within a saturated airmass (precipitable water 2.18) produced locally heavy, flooding rainfall.
episodes.193481: A severe thunderstorm moved northeast across central Fall River County, producing wind gusts to around 60 mph.
episodes.193776: A broken line of thunderstorms developed over the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of July 27th. As this activity moved to the southeast, it produced wind gusts to 60 MPH in western Cherry and Lincoln counties.
episodes.194139: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over Mellette County, producing wind gusts to 70 mph over the White River area.
episodes.194730: A high based thunderstorm produced a 69 mph wind gust at the Greybull airport.
episodes.194824: Deep monsoonal moisture pushed in from the west during the overnight and early morning hours accompanied by a shortwave disturbance, allowing for stronger storms to form capable of heavy rainfall rates. This moisture replaced a previously dry air mass so heavy rain threat was more localized. One particular storm resulted in debris flows over Pitkin County that evening.
episodes.194866: After a stalled boundary set up across northwestern Minnesota across the river into North Dakota, thunderstorms and showers trained over the same area in the frontal zone, leading to flash flooding in some areas.
episodes.194994: A cut off mid-level low pressure system resulted in a swirl of moisture advecting west over western Missouri and eastern Kansas on July 27, 2024. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed throughout the day, with a thunderstorm producing heavy rainfall over Phelps County.
episodes.195162: A deep trough stretched across South Texas into Mexico, leading to favorable conditions for efficient rainfall over the Coastal Bend. Greatest rainfall occurred on July 25th, with over 10 falling in just 6 hours over North Padre Island and rainfall rates up to 4 an hour. Several reports of streets flooded along Padre Island and in poor drainage areas of Corpus Christi.
episodes.195190: Deep monsoon moisture triggered strong to severe thunderstorms with hail and heavy rain over parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.195224: In the middle of a monsoonal surge, plenty of deep moisture was available to fuel showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 27th. In addition, modest instability and enhanced lift and shear from an upper level jet were also in place, leading to an increased chance of stronger storms forming. The Storm Prediction Center place the region under a marginal risk for severe weather, highlight severe wind and hail threats. The hail did not materialize, but the winds did.
episodes.195246: Several wind gusts over 50 knots recorded in southeast Idaho.

events.narrative: A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall rates resulting in a large mudslide at Avalanche Ranch along Highway 133.  There were other mudslides along Highway 133 between Redstone Blvd and Red Dog Rd about 4 miles north of Redstone. These mudslides resulted in Highway 133 being closed in both directions from mile markers 53 to 57.

Thunderstorms tracked across Rio Blanco and Routt counties on the afternoon of the 27th, producing strong to severe wind gusts as they did so. Recorded wind gusts ranged from 50 mph to 60  mph, with the peak gust being recorded at the PIRC2 Pinto mesonet site, 18 miles southeast of Massadona. Gusts into the 50s were recorded at KEEO ASOS at Meeker Airport and KHDN AWOS at Yampa Valley Airport in Hayden. No reports of damages or injuries were received.
